sections.html:
Kootenai County is in the Idaho Panhandle, and Coeur d'Alene serves as both county seat and largest city. The population has roughly tripled since 1980, from 59,770 to an estimated 191,864 in 2025. Newer subdivisions around Post Falls and Rathdrum now sit near older housing close to the lake and downtown.

Fourteen incorporated cities share the county, among them Athol, Coeur d'Alene, Dalton Gardens, Hayden, Post Falls, Rathdrum and Spirit Lake. A seller's address might be inside a city, on the water or on rural land, and the rules that apply change with each. Growth shows up in the tax rolls too, since districts keep adjusting to a bigger base of homes. Many residents also work across the state line, with 5,031 county residents holding jobs in Spokane, Washington.

The county uses its own snow load map and its own amendments to the building code, so a roof is measured against a local standard. The residential permit guide sets a minimum frost depth of 24 inches for footings, and the county adopted its current construction codes by Ordinance 608, effective January 1, 2020.

Manufactured and mobile homes get specific treatment under Title 7 of the county code. A legally set home that meets county and state rules can be relocated without extra proof if it can be verified as built for a roof snow load of at least 30 pounds per square foot. If you are selling one, gather the data plate and any permits before you list.

Missing permits tend to surface at the worst moment, right after an inspection. Ask the county building office what permits are on file for a finished basement, a deck or a shop before a buyer asks. Older homes near the lake tend to draw closer looks at the roof, wiring and foundation.

The county mails every tax notice by the fourth Monday of November. Payment is due on or before December 20. Not getting a bill does not excuse the tax, under Idaho Code 63-902(9).

Payment methodHow it works
MailCounts as on time only with a USPS postmark on or before the due date
In personPay at the counter instead of by mail
OnlineCredit card at kcgov.us; the payer covers transaction fees
Phone208-446-1005, option 3

Interest on delinquent tax runs at one percent per month starting January 1. Treat the December 20 date as firm, and note that an appeal does not pause payment.

sections.h2: What happens after three years unpaid?
sections.html:
Kootenai County follows a tax deed track. Once real property taxes are three years delinquent, the tax collector sends the recorded owner a Pending Issue of Tax Deed letter. To stop the process, the owner must pay the third year in full. Partial payments are applied to the balance but do not stop it.

An owner who cannot pay can apply to the Board of County Commissioners for hardship relief at 208-446-1600. Parcels that reach the end of the process go to a tax deed auction. If this describes your house, an early sale or payoff through escrow protects whatever equity you have.

The deadline is the fourth Monday in June. The only way to file is through the Board of County Commissioners' office at 208-446-1600. The Board of Equalization hearing runs like a court and acts in a quasi-judicial role, so prepare accordingly.

Bring evidence that the assessed value is wrong: a recent appraisal, repair estimates or documentation of damage. Keep paying on schedule while the appeal is open.

Two offices split the work, and calling the wrong one costs time. The assessor handles value and appeals. The treasurer handles bills, payments and delinquencies.

The Recorder charges $10 for the first page and $3 for each additional page of standard documents. Surveys are $5.00 a page, plats are $11.00 and copies of recorded documents are $1.00 a page. State law sets a $15.00 fee for deeds of 30 pages or less. The office is open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding holidays.

If an heir, a divorcing spouse or a co-owner is involved, record the deed before the sale instead of waiting for closing. The title company then has the full chain of ownership in hand.

Sorting out which office answers which question saves a lot of back and forth. Here is a short directory built from the numbers above.

  • Tax balance, payment questions and payoff totals: the treasurer, 208-446-1005.
  • Appeals and hardship relief: the Board of County Commissioners' office, 208-446-1600.
  • Permits on file for a deck, shop or finished basement: the county building office.
  • Deed recording and copies of recorded documents: the Recorder, open weekdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Write down who you spoke with and what number they gave you. If a payoff figure will be used at closing, ask for it in writing so the title company can match it to the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Getting the house ready for a sale
sections.html:
Buyers in North Idaho look hard at anything tied to weather. Have the roof checked against the local snow load standard if the house is older, and know the age of the heating system. If you own a manufactured home, find the data plate early, since it is the document that proves the roof snow load rating.

Property tax is the other half of the file. Print the treasurer's balance, confirm both halves are current and keep the mailing postmark or receipt for any payment you made by mail. A clean tax record tells a buyer the house has no hidden liens waiting at closing, and it lets a cash buyer or an agent quote a firm timeline.

If the house sits on a lake, on rural land or inside a smaller city such as Athol or Spirit Lake, ask the title company whether any additional district or city charges appear on the bill. Rules differ by address, and the surprise is usually in the details of a particular parcel.

sections.h2: Closing day on a Kootenai County sale
sections.html:
Plan the last week backward from the title company's closing date. Confirm the payoff total a few days ahead, not that morning. Gather the deed information, any lake or rural parcel details and the names of everyone on title, because a co-owner who is missing from the paperwork can delay recording.

After closing, the recorder files the deed and the treasurer's records follow. Hold on to your copy of the settlement statement and one confirmation that taxes were paid, so a later question about a bill has a paper trail.

You can sell a house with unpaid property tax. Call the treasurer at 208-446-1005 for an exact payoff total, then have the title or escrow company pay it out of your proceeds. The county warns that escrow may not pay the treasurer if closing happens before annual tax information is available, so confirm in writing that the tax is actually paid after closing.

A typical sequence looks like this:

  1. Get the payoff total from the treasurer.
  2. Tell the title company about every unpaid year, not only the current one.
  3. Ask whether the closing falls before or after annual tax information is released.
  4. Keep your settlement statement and a receipt from the treasurer.

When a deed process is looming, speed matters, and a cash purchase removes the wait for a buyer's loan approval. We take houses in whatever shape they are in, and turning an offer down costs you nothing. Set it beside what a listing would put in your pocket before choosing.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Kootenai County?
faqs.a: Coeur d'Alene is both the county seat and the largest city.

faqs.q: When are Kootenai County property tax bills mailed?
faqs.a: Notices go out by the fourth Monday of November, and the tax is payable on or before December 20.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Kootenai County property assessment?
faqs.a: Contact the Board of County Commissioners' office at 208-446-1600 by the fourth Monday in June. The hearing before the Board of Equalization works like a court proceeding.

faqs.q: What happens after three years of unpaid property tax in Kootenai County?
faqs.a: The tax collector sends the recorded owner a Pending Issue of Tax Deed letter. Paying the third year in full stops the process, and partial payments do not.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Kootenai County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Get the exact payoff from the treasurer at 208-446-1005 and have the title or escrow company pay it from your proceeds. Escrow may not pay the treasurer if closing comes before annual tax information is available.
